reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it provides practical Mac malware prevention and removal guidance, including password, application-download, and running-software checks. The infection pop-up, repair demand, phone contact, remote-access scenario, and password prompt are presented as examples of users being fooled, followed by warnings not to call, pay, or provide card information. The Abt website and Apple-product reference indicate ordinary business promotion that is not explicitly connected to the suspicious actors or scenarios.

citations.quote: You're just getting conned by a pop-up. That says you're infected, you have a virus,. You need to do this and download this program. To clean it up.
they get fooled,. And they download it, and they install something,. And next thing they know, they're calling a phone number,. And they want $299 to fix the virus.
These are not Apple, Apple doesn't do that. So be cautious when the phone number pops up,. Don't call it, don't pay anyone anything. Or give them your credit card.
What if you accidentally called the phone number. And they logged into your computer. And they showed you all sorts of things?
And it looks legit like you have an issue. So they try to scare you. And they want that credit card number.

opening.argument: The content links a viewer action to a commercial pathway: viewers are told to visit Abt's website, inspect the Apple products it carries, and local customers are encouraged to contact Abt's technicians. That makes the malware-help framing function partly as a solicitation for outside engagement and potentially product or service acquisition. The video does not establish a free reward or income opportunity, but the combination of a problem-focused pitch and a directed next step is consistent with a low-barrier acquisition funnel that deserves scrutiny.

you can always seek out professional support like at Apt.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense calls the website ordinary promotion, but that is precisely the concern: the warning is embedded in a commercial channel and directs viewers toward the seller's products and support. The educational framing does not establish that the requested visit is unrelated to acquisition. Nor does describing malicious callers prove that Abt's own solicitation is harmless; it leaves the commercial purpose of the surrounding appeal intact.

citations.quote: Be sure to visit www.abt.com for more info and to check out the different Apple products we carry!

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The cited website invitation expressly says to check out Apple products, but it does not promise a free reward, income, withdrawal, or asset. The support reference offers removal tools through a named service group, not a reward for completing a task. Those quotes show ordinary product and service promotion, not the low-barrier reward mechanism required for this category.

citations.quote: to check out the different Apple products we carry!
our Connect Tech group is going to be able to offer malicious software removal tools

opening.argument: Several concrete scam-like mechanisms appear together: a pop-up claims infection and directs a download, installation is followed by a phone call and a demand for $299, and a caller may seek a credit-card number after making the problem look legitimate. Those are unusually direct action-and-payment signals. Even if presented as warnings, the material supplies a ready-made sequence of infection claim, software action, phone contact, and payment request; a careful judge cannot treat the presence of those mechanisms as irrelevant merely because the speaker criticizes them.

citations.quote: You're just getting conned by a pop-up. That says you're infected, you have a virus,. You need to do this and download this program. To clean it up.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense emphasizes warnings, but the quoted material still presents a detailed, credible-looking payment pathway: infection claim, download, installation, phone contact, and $299 demand. Calling the actors deceptive does not erase the commercial mechanics being described. The speaker also acknowledges that the fake problem can look legitimate, so viewers are being exposed to a persuasive solicitation pattern rather than merely abstract security advice.

citations.quote: And next thing they know, they're calling a phone number,. And they want $299 to fix the virus.
And it looks legit like you have an issue.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: These quotes describe people being fooled, not the speaker asking viewers to download software, call a number, or pay $299. The surrounding instruction explicitly identifies the conduct as fraudulent and tells viewers not to participate. A described scam mechanism is not itself a solicitation, and the evidence does not show that the video promises viewers any reward or asset for acting.

citations.quote: You're just getting conned by a pop-up.
Don't call it, don't pay anyone anything. Or give them your credit card.

opening.argument: Although presented as security education, the video repeatedly directs viewers toward Abt's commercial ecosystem. The speaker identifies Abt as an Apple service center and seller, promotes its support group, and the description sends viewers to the company website to inspect products. The malware-warning role therefore also operates as promotional content that turns fear about computer problems into a reason to contact the business or consider its offerings. That commercial steering is the closest available fit to an acquisition-oriented scam classification, even though no reward is promised.

citations.quote: Now Abt is an authorized Apple service center as well as sales.

our Connect Tech group is going to be able to offer malicious software removal tools

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense treats the business references as incidental, but they are repeated alongside the malware problem and a direct website invitation. A viewer concerned about infection is steered toward the same company for products and technical help. Calling that ordinary promotion does not answer whether the warning is being used to generate commercial participation.

citations.quote: we're one of those dealers that you can trust that sells and supports Apple.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The commercial references identify the source and available services, but they do not promise a free or unusually easy reward, income, withdrawal, or digital asset. The warning's substantive instructions tell viewers to avoid suspicious downloads, phone numbers, payments, and credit-card disclosure. Product promotion may be present, but it does not create the required reward-for-action relationship.
